body:
I'm not sure I like the new 'use vertex color' option. My first thought is you added it as the current default for vertex colors completely overrides the color property if VC data exists at the correct array length. In some sense, it'd probably be better to only create/manage this VC data if the user has enabled it in some way.

 _

I'm not sure the best way to handle an alternative to the checkbox, but if possible, I think the easiest way to fix would be if the default *wasn't* a color but just loads\* from the color property itself (allowing color variants and shading with an easily changeable base color), perhaps even listing this as 'none'. Though I also think an actual color index system would be really useful, especially with multiple layers.

I'm split though, because I do see that checkbox could be useful. For instance, I could see someone having flat-shaded characters that turn VC on when they're angry or something like that. I just personally am not sure I'll use it that way.

In either case I think it would be useful if VC could be saved as an external resource, so they can be swapped out/shared more easily. Though that is probably beyond this PR, likely something other teams talk about (it would probably need an editor icon, extension etc). 

--------------------------------

I also feel like painting in the main editor would be my choice, though using a dedicated editor also feels fine too (especially if you can get color rendering there). 

Probably just odd for me as historically, the UV editor would yell at you rather than open if you didn't have a texture on your polygon (despite the points section etc). EDIT: emphasis on historically, that was fixed years ago and even the version I use isn't like that now

-------------------------------

\* loading from color *was* the old system (when out-of-index), though IIRC the issue was that you'd need to edit the polygon in such a way that point 0..needed was where you wanted your vertex color

> I'm not sure the best way to handle an alternative to the checkbox, but if possible, I think the easiest way to fix would be if the default _wasn't_ a color but just loads* from the color property itself (allowing color variants and shading with an easily changeable base color), perhaps even listing this as 'none'. Though I also think an actual color index system would be really useful, especially with multiple layers.

Figuring out how to automatically assign the right color from the property as the vertex color array changes size was in fact considered, but ended up being too complicated to implement in practice.

> I'm split though, because I do see that checkbox could be useful. For instance, I could see someone having flat-shaded characters that turn VC on when they're angry or something like that. I just personally am not sure I'll use it that way.

This was generally the idea. Also so that the data could still be called upon for other game logic or shader trickery even if the coloring isn't being directly applied, because in a fair number of 3D games, vertex color data on meshes have been used for things that aren't necessarily coloring for interesting effects. How this can work for shaders specifically though, I have yet to test.

> In either case I think it would be useful if VC could be saved as an external resource, so they can be swapped out/shared more easily. Though that is probably beyond this PR, likely something other teams talk about (it would probably need an editor icon, extension etc).

I would like this too, also for sharing the polygon data itself as a resource.  Still beyond the scope of what I want to get done for the moment.

> I also feel like painting in the main editor would be my choice, though using a dedicated editor also feels fine too (especially if you can get color rendering there).

I also agree that the polygon editor plugin should have more parity in what could be seen/done through the scene viewport and the dedicated editor tab. This is an issue not entirely exclusive to my vertex color editing features though, and I want to attempt to tackle that separately.

Right now my mindset is I would rather make small incremental improvements focusing on one part of Polygon2D editing/usage at a time, because having a very simple implementation of a feature is still better than not having it at all. 
I don't want people waiting an eternity for the basics of a feature when any hypothetical improvements tangentially related to it can simply be figured out afterwards.

> Figuring out how to automatically assign the right color from the property as the vertex color array changes size was in fact considered, but ended up being too complicated to implement in practice.

Understandable, though I am talking about even before array changes. My point is that:

a. you shouldn't be creating/managing data before it has been enabled
b. static default data is not (and cannot) be useful here, and even copying data isn't great either if that isn't continuously managed too
c. requiring manual changes is an issue that scales with the number of vertices and complexity of design(s)\*.

A micro-step could be to restore the 3.0 out-of-bounds VC map behavior (assuming viable) but then add an index offset (or even rotate index instead?). Not perfect (cannot handle non-contiguous\*\* vertex color), but covers some basics.

\* admittedly this is even an issue with Blender's vertex painting, albeit mitigated with other tools like select-by-material, selection tools (depending on mesh design + user knowledge), and vertex groups(?)

\*\* Unless the color could simply be un-assigned (set to null) per-index?

As far as I know, the vertex color array cannot have any entries with null values.* I'm not even sure if you can set a Color to null at all in Godot If you could, that would easily provide my preferred solution. I do see the point you're making now, though. It would be nice if vertex coloring could work while vertices without a color assignment default on the "color" property's value. 

At the very least it should be easy to disable the synchronization of vertex array and color array sizes until "use vertex colors" is turned on (and ~~maybe put up a warning in or~~ disable the vertex painting tab when it's turned off to make things clear for end users). ~~Will get to work on that as soon as I have the time.~~ **

Also will look into how vertex coloring is applied under the hood some more, in case there is a clean enough way to do what you describe.

*okay, so I have all but confirmed 'Color's simply cannot have a null value. I'm willing to bet that changing that would be a very big deal, and I would like to have the opinion of more of the engine's core dev team on the matter. Perhaps changing the type of 'vertex_colors' to a dictionary/hashmap of some kind would be preferable? The keys could track which vertices to apply color values to. It would keep the data size down to a minimum, at least.

** done
Going forward with the idea of exposing a Typed Dictionary to the editor to define which vertices have a color that overrides the "Color" property.

Pretty happy with how this painting tool works now. No longer requires manually enabling/disabling vertex coloring. It is now able to fall back on the default Color property for vertices without a defined color. I also added an eraser tool.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0df436e3-912e-463c-83a9-792e01c97fb0

There is but one more thing I want to tackle before I think this is ready for review again, and that's making sure that vertex color assignments are preserved positionally when using the abstract polygon2d editor to insert a new point along an edge.

Otherwise this happens, which would be really annoying to deal with if you want to edit the polygon after coloring.
It's far from the only quality-of-life improvement I'd like to make to Polygon2D editing, but this is all I think should be within the scope of this PR.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d24a6fd1-7664-4c34-be95-b46aa73b895a

>There is but one more thing I want to tackle before I think this is ready for review again, and that's making sure that vertex color assignments are preserved positionally when using the abstract polygon2d editor to insert a new point along an edge.

I believe that's mission accomplished. The new points that are inserted still leave their vertex color unassigned, and I'm not sure if people would want that or if I should assign it a blend of the two colors between it. Regardless, the results are far less painful to deal with now.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ecfc6aa2-ced3-4e34-a97b-cd80af7b060c

> I'm not sure if people would want that or if I should assign it a blend of the two colors between it

I have been working on my own 3-digit-hex color palette (12-bit-rgb or 15-level-per-channel, e.g. `#ac3` --> `#aacc33`). I wouldn't much appreciate colors being muddied to 6-digit accidentally, although I have made my own conversion shader so when using that it wouldn't be so bad (still 12-bit, but no longer conforming to palette).

In either case, you could safely detect same-color or even choose one-or-the-other for differing colors (particularly when it's not perfectly in the middle).


>I don't want people waiting an eternity for the basics of a feature when any hypothetical improvements tangentially related to it can simply be figured out afterwards.

My mindset is that big/many changes are a lot easier to notice and a lot more forgivable when it comes to breaking compatibility. You are of course right though, and I fully understand given my issue is from 2019 and that I've done enough programming to know it's not that easy.

-----------

I just want to add that color display would further make sense in the editor when users also have a texture enabled (color+texture display in the viewport, but only color in the editor) though this definitely could be added later.

-----------

Also, did you change your mind completely on ability to disable VC display? I should say the bit about technical usage was something I've only thought about for 3D (and I'm also not sure if they'd use it polygon2D or something like meshinstance2D especially if it's a generated map) but you are right that there are use-cases. My original negativity was more on the context (resulting in it disabled by default) that you've already fixed.

Unless there is some alternate way, at least to disable colors for effects as I mentioned? Aside from manually changing every set color, can you animate the dictionary to be disabled (set dictionary as one key/animation track, blank dictionary as another key)? Or maybe you change the vert index to all the same index in such a way that the one that gets rendered is the right color?

You mentioned shaders and I very much agree, I could see some things like this using per-instance parameters if it were easy to do so. Though also future changes that I've mentioned would make it easier too.

>You mentioned shaders and I very much agree, I could see some things like this using per-instance parameters if it were easy to do so. Though also future changes that I've mentioned would make it easier too.

I found out that the GPU isn't really going to have direct access to the data inside the dictionary regardless, because under the hood, the data from the default color value and vertex data gets melted down to a single list that gets sent to the renderer.

If you want to do something different with the vertex color data and color it another way, there's still a way to do that in shader code without a "disable" checkbox in the editor.

Knowing this, I thought the use-case for such a checkbox was quite a bit more niche than my initial appraisal, and would probably confuse people trying to work with shaders.
Seems C# bindings don't like the hint, unsure if it's formatted incorrectly or if it just doesn't handle this case

> Seems C# bindings don't like the hint, unsure if it's formatted incorrectly or if it just doesn't handle this case

I could see either being the case yea. Last I checked there wasn't any other place in the code where a TypedDictionary is exposed to the editor, let alone with such granular property hinting.
Maybe I could try another way of formatting it that achieves the same result, see if that helps any.
Please try using `TypedDictionary<int64_t, Color>` instead, it might have an issue with the unusual use of `uint32_t`

> Please try using `TypedDictionary<int64_t, Color>` instead, it might have an issue with the unusual use of `uint32_t`

it just occurred to me that seemingly all integer values intended to be exposed to the editor are simply an `int` internally. It may be wiser to try that instead.

They are not generally `int` I'd say (or rather not universally), they are often `int64_t` which would be the appropriate type, unless there's some reason to restrict it? The original wasn't as far as I can tell? So I'd say to use `int64_t`

Edit: I'm not sure the hint is really needed in any case, again as there was no such restrictions before AFAIK, it just used `Vector` which has an index range of `int64_t`, the practical limit of the size of the vertex index aside it wasn't enforced (and was `int32_t`, not `uint32_t`)

> Edit: I'm not sure the hint is really needed in any case

I was also thinking that as I was writing the changes. Double-checking the code that iterates through the dictionary to apply the coloring, I'm not seeing anything that could cause actual problems if someone manually entered key values that are negative or really large or anything. I was just being paranoid.
May as well remove that part of the property hinting just to be doubly sure the C# bindings will generate properly.
If the change to `int64_t` fixes it the range hint can be left as it is, as it helps users with the valid range I'd say

Since neither of those ideas worked, I've tried generating the mono glue on my local copy to look at the output myself. It seems unlikely it was tripping up on property hints. The affected area mostly has to do with the compatibility methods. Still investigating, will get back to you on this.
I think it's down to the bindings not handling `TypedDictionary` properties, try changing to `Dictionary` and keep the hint, that's how other properties do it

> I think it's down to the bindings not handling `TypedDictionary` properties, try changing to `Dictionary` and keep the hint, that's how other properties do it (Update: I have confirmed this is even the case when the int type is `uint_32_t`) The output of glue generation in `Polygon2D.cs` is actually able to parse the typing perfectly when using TypedDictionary. (this is how you normally declare a typed Dictionary in C# and it checks out) The property hints weren't affecting the output either. as I said, the real problem is down here where it tries to implement the backwards compatibility methods it seems to be unhappy about the highlighted part where it declares "colors". I've never seen anything like this before, and nothing we tried so far affects this part of the output. (Yes I tried changing the type to a plain Dictionary anyways to test if it changed anything, no dice) my guess is that it's failing to parse the `&p_colors` parameter in the equivalent C++ function somehow.

>my guess is that it's failing to parse the &p_colors parameter in the equivalent C++ function somehow.

I figured it out. I needed to change
``ClassDB::bind_compatibility_method(D_METHOD("set_vertex_colors, colors"), &Polygon2D::_set_vertex_colors_118023);``
to
``ClassDB::bind_compatibility_method(D_METHOD("set_vertex_colors", "colors"), &Polygon2D::_set_vertex_colors_118023);``

I messed up the quotation marks and comma placements. The glue generated locally in my testing is now valid.

While I'm at it, I'd like to say "thank you" to all parties involved for being so patient with my foolhardy yet earnest attempts to learn the ins and outs of contributing to this project. I know things have gotten way more difficult for maintainers lately with all the bogus AI-generated PRs.

Assuming the uint --> int change stays in, does a negative index already have a defined behavior?Because if *those* didn't display... that sounds like a much easier way to animate effects\*, as well as an easy way for code to have readable\*\* color that isn't displayed (not via GPU, but this is my assumption when in a script anyway) like for footstep sounds.

\* for instance if you use VC for an eye sclera (or a traffic light), setting index of those points to negative would be a dead-simple way to make a 'blink' animation. Even point-by-point. Where this would get shaky would be that adding that functionality to the painting tool as well (hide/show?) particularly if it's to be used for more complex effect (say, eye/mouth *shapes* with multiple internal points that'd be a pain to edit via the inspector)

\*\* direct from dictionary, as it wouldn't be sent to VC

> Assuming the uint --> int change stays in, does a negative index already have a defined behavior?Because if _those_ didn't display... that sounds like a much easier way to animate effects*, as well as an easy way for code to have readable** color that isn't displayed (not via GPU, but this is my assumption when in a script anyway) like for footstep sounds.

Key values below 0 would simply be ignored by any loop in the editor tools and draw function that iterates through the dictionary since the loop counts up from 0. It should be completely safe to have them, but would be highly impractical to use them for anything. There are countless more straightforward ways to accomplish any of those things you described. 
Dictionary lookups/edits can be very expensive performance-wise and scale poorly, so it would be wise to minimize how often you have to do them. I was a bit apprehensive about changing the type of the ``vertex_colors`` property in the first place for this exact reason, but resolved that it might be ok since it's mostly for the editor tools, and the draw function that melts the dictionary down before feeding it to the rendering server would (I think) only be called so often if the dictionary isn't constantly changing.
Ergo, a shader is still ideal for doing any fancy animations or effects with vertex colors.

> it would be wise to minimize how often you have to do them

Yeah. I was already thinking 1-12FPS frame-by-frame animation _bursts_, state changes, as well as low iteration count (main characters, cutscenes, setpieces). Very stylized. (and yeah, many things could be done with additional nodes, in some cases it may have redundant data though)

Lookups for maps probably could just be done once when loading and stored.
